channelTitle: The museum has a wall of letters that all say the same thing: I'm sorry, Robert - Part 2
hook: In Part 1, Gene Otto spent his whole life insisting his doll Robert was more than straw and cloth. In Part 2, the museum finds out what that means.
storyParts: Gene died in nineteen seventy-four. The new owners of the house reported footsteps in the empty attic, giggling in the walls, and a plumber who refused to go back upstairs. They gave Robert away - to the East Martello Museum.
The museum put him in a glass case in the old fort, sailor suit and all - and within months, odd things started getting reported by visitors who leaned in close to take his picture.
Cameras failing, batteries draining dead, photos coming out blurred - but only around Robert's case. Staff noticed a pattern and began a small tradition: writing apology letters to the doll.
Now the wall beside his case is covered - thousands of letters, all saying roughly the same thing: I mocked you, then bad things happened, and I am sorry. Flights missed, jobs lost, cars wrecked.
Skeptics say it is suggestion plus an old doll's cracked painted face doing the work. Maybe so - but every year Robert gets more mail than most living people do in a lifetime.
cta: Would you dare write a joke letter to Robert, or play it safe like everyone else? Tell Grandma June below.
moral: Haunted or not, Robert proves one thing - a well-told story can keep a stranger polite for a hundred years.
seriesTitle: Robert the Doll - Grandma June Story Time
